import numpy as np

def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    steps = 60
    dt = duration_s / (steps - 1)

    lat = np.full(n_runs, start[0], dtype=np.float64)
    lon = np.full(n_runs, start[1], dtype=np.float64)
    time = np.zeros(n_runs, dtype=np.float64)

    points = np.zeros((n_runs, steps, 3), dtype=np.float64)
    points[:, 0, 0] = lat
    points[:, 0, 1] = lon
    points[:, 0, 2] = 0

    ok = np.ones(n_runs, dtype=bool)

    # Precompute meters-per-degree for scale
    m_lat = terrain.m_lat
    m_lon = terrain.m_lon
    cell_m = terrain.cell_m

    # helper to convert lat/lon increments to meters offsets and back
    def meters_to_deg_lat(d_m):
        return d_m / m_lat
    def meters_to_deg_lon(d_m):
        return d_m / m_lon

    # At each step:
    #  1) We want to go roughly north along the game trail direction
    #  2) Sampling terrain in a sector, select direction toward closest saddle
    # A saddle is a low point on ridgeline, so roughly a local minimum transverse to main direction

    # Strategy:
    #   At each step, sample directions in [north +/- 40 deg], e.g. 9 points at 10 deg steps
    #   For each sampled bearing:
    #       - offset ~15m along that bearing (half cell)
    #       - get elevation and slope
    #       - compute elevation profile to identify saddles:
    #         here approximate saddle likelihood as low slope and elevation lower than neighbor points
    #       - Also get distance to trail (prefer closer to trail)

    # Select direction with minimal elevation and low slope, closer to trail

    n_angles = 9
    bearing_offsets = np.linspace(-40, +40, n_angles) * np.pi / 180  # radians offset from north (0 rad)
    north_bearing = 0

    # Precompute starting elevation and to_trail
    elev = terrain.elev(lat, lon)
    to_trail = terrain.to_trail(lat, lon)

    for step in range(1, steps):
        # Sample bearing candidates
        candidate_bearings = north_bearing + bearing_offsets[None, :]  # shape (1, n_angles)

        # Broadcast current positions to n_angles each
        lat_rep = lat[:, None]  # (n_runs,1)
        lon_rep = lon[:, None]  # (n_runs,1)

        # Offset ~15m along candidate bearings
        dist_sample = 15.0
        lat_cands, lon_cands = terrain.offset(lat_rep, lon_rep, candidate_bearings, dist_sample)  # (n_runs, n_angles)

        # Clamp points inside terrain box
        lat_cands, lon_cands = terrain.clamp(lat_cands, lon_cands)

        # Elevation and slope at candidates
        elev_cands = terrain.elev(lat_cands, lon_cands)
        slope_cands = terrain.slope_deg(lat_cands, lon_cands)
        trail_cands = terrain.to_trail(lat_cands, lon_cands)

        # "Saddle score":
        # Low slope (prefer <15 deg)
        # Elevation lower than current elev (encourage downward or flat)
        # Closer to trail (smaller better)
        # Compose a score normalized by ranges:
        #   slope_score = slope_cands/90 (0 to 1)
        #   elev_score = (elev_cands - elev[:,None]) / max(1, np.ptp(elev_cands, axis=1, keepdims=True))
        #   elev_score clipped to -1..1 for stability
        #   trail_score normalized by max across candidates
        slope_score = slope_cands / 90.0
        elev_diff = elev_cands - elev[:, None]
        elev_range = np.ptp(elev_cands, axis=1, keepdims=True)
        elev_range[elev_range < 1] = 1
        elev_norm = elev_diff / elev_range
        elev_norm = np.clip(elev_norm, -1, 1)
        trail_norm = trail_cands / np.maximum(np.ptp(trail_cands, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1)

        score = slope_score + elev_norm + trail_norm

        # Choose bearing with minimal score (prefer lower)
        idx_sel = np.argmin(score, axis=1)

        # Selected bearing per run
        bearing_sel = candidate_bearings[0, idx_sel]

        # Compute distance can travel this step:
        # velocity from Tobler function:
        # Calculate elevation delta along selected bearing:
        # approximated by difference between elev_cands[np.arange(n_runs), idx_sel] and elev
        elev_sel = elev_cands[np.arange(n_runs), idx_sel]
        delta_elev = elev_sel - elev

        d_horiz = dist_sample

        speed = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(delta_elev, d_horiz)  # m/s

        dist_walk = speed * dt
        # limit step distance to dist_sample (we only sampled candidates at dist_sample)
        dist_walk = np.minimum(dist_walk, dist_sample)

        # Move along bearing_sel by dist_walk
        lat_new, lon_new = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearing_sel, dist_walk)
        lat_new, lon_new = terrain.clamp(lat_new, lon_new)

        # Update time
        time += dt

        # Save
        points[:, step, 0] = lat_new
        points[:, step, 1] = lon_new
        points[:, step, 2] = time

        # Update for next step
        lat, lon = lat_new, lon_new
        elev = terrain.elev(lat, lon)
        to_trail = terrain.to_trail(lat, lon)

        # Mark ok where inside; once false, stays false
        inside = terrain.inside(lat, lon)
        ok = ok & inside

    return points, ok

hypothesis.rationale: Experienced hikers sometimes seek natural passes that ridgelines offer.
